**Palm et al., 2020** is a pivotal medical meta-analysis that provides the primary evidence base for the clinical effectiveness of [[patientuddannelse|Patientuddannelse]] (patient education) in patients with atrial fibrillation. Published in 2020, the study serves as a cornerstone document for evidence-based healthcare quality development in Denmark, specifically acting as the foundational justification for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] (structured patient education) in the national atrial fibrillation quality reports (AFDK) [^src1] [^src2].

The meta-analysis synthesized data from five randomized controlled trials and one non-randomized intervention study, encompassing a total of 2,007 patients [^src1] [^src2]. The researchers found that patients who received structured education experienced a statistically significant 22% reduction in the combined risk of death and hospital readmission compared to control groups receiving no education (Risk Ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.63–0.97) [^src1] [^src2]. 

Within the broader narrative of the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP), this publication bridges international standards—such as the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines and the ABC Pathway model—with national clinical practices [^src2]. By quantifying the tangible clinical outcomes of patient-centered education, Palm et al. (2020) transformed patient education from a theoretical best practice into a measurable, evidence-based quality indicator that drives systematic cardiovascular care improvements across Danish regions [^src1] [^src2].
